key_insight: AT-SKM-Net speeds up hard-constraint feasibility solving on dynamic graphs by learning which constraints to sample and updating projections efficiently without losing zero-violation guarantees.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets large-scale infrastructure optimization problems where strict feasibility and fast adaptation to graph changes are critical, such as power grids and gas transport.
method: Hybrid sampling guided by a topology-aware heterogeneous GNN to focus computation on active constraints
Cholesky update mechanism for low-rank topology changes, reducing equality projection cost from O(N^3) to O(N^2)
Projection-based trainable SKM framework designed to preserve feasibility while accelerating iterations
evidence_signal: Across random geometric graphs, N-1 security-constrained DC-OPF, and minimum-cost gas transport benchmarks, the method reports up to 85% fewer iterations, 2.95x–7.29x faster SKM layers, and zero constraint violations.
watch_item: Performance likely depends on the quality of the learned sampling policy and on assumptions that graph perturbations are low-rank enough for efficient Cholesky updates.
paper_title: AT-SKM-Net: An Accelerated Trainable Sampling Kaczmarz-Motzkin Framework for Linear Hard-Constraint Feasibility on Dynamic Graphs
